verdict.rationale: Homebrew's first-party docs describe committing a Brewfile to a project repository to declare its dependencies. Users then run a single command (`brew bundle` / `brew bundle install`) to install everything it lists: formulae, casks, taps and other package types. A documented `brew bundle check || brew bundle install` idiom supports scripted and CI bootstrapping. missing for 10: independent or hands-on corroboration that `brew bundle` reliably bootstraps a fresh clone.

support.subject: As a developer, I can bootstrap a fresh clone with one command that installs everything the project declares

citations.quote: Adding a `Brewfile` to a project's repository (like you might a `package.json`, `Gemfile` or `requirements.txt`) is a nicer way of encoding project dependencies for developer environments.
It allows you to tell users to run a single command to install all dependencies for a project and start any services.
one command can set up project dependencies across these environments and in continuous-integration services such as GitHub Actions.
You can use this behaviour in scripts like so: brew bundle check || brew bundle install
